ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own sanctions list (e.g., the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list of designated persons). Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by FATF, including family members and close associates. Screening must be performed at onboarding and on an ongoing basis, with automated alerts and manual review. Any positive match triggers immediate suspension of the formation process and filing of a suspicious transaction report (STR) with KoFIU. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea's Commercial Registration System (i-REG, 인터넷등기소) at https://www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean script (Hangul). English names may be used as a secondary name but must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul. The name must consist of a distinctive element, a business purpose descriptor, and a legal form suffix (e.g., '주식회사' for stock company, '유한회사' for LLC). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. Four-tier naming conventions: (1) distinctive word, (2) business type, (3) legal form, (4) optional English transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registry within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be in writing, stating the grounds for reconsideration, and must include a certified copy of the rejection notice. The Registry must respond within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Administrative Court within 90 days. Alternatively, the applicant may modify the name and resubmit. The appeal process is governed by the Commercial Registration Act and the Administrative Litigation Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally permissible for registration purposes, but Korean tax authorities (NTS) and banks may require a physical presence for certain activities. For a cybersecurity SaaS company, a virtual office may be accepted for registration, but banks may require a physical address for account opening and may conduct on-site inspections. The NTS may reject a virtual office if it lacks commercial substance, especially if the company claims tax incentives or has high transaction volumes. It is recommended to have a physical office or a serviced office with a dedicated address and staff to ensure compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) NTS may conduct unannounced inspections to verify the existence of the registered office. (2) The registry may also verify the address. (3) Banks may conduct on-site inspections during account opening. (4) The likelihood is moderate for a low-risk SaaS company, but increases if the company is flagged for any reason. Quantified risk: 20% chance of inspection within the first year, rising to 50% if the company claims tax incentives or has high transaction volumes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 543 through 568 governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), together with Articles 288, 295, 296, 317 and 601 on incorporation, registration, directors and registration procedure, the Local Tax Act Articles 24 through 28 on registration tax, and the Commercial Registration Rules of the Supreme Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, or the District Court Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office in the Republic of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation and the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (corporate registration filing under Article 547 of the Commercial Act).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. A Yuhan Hoesa has no statutory minimum paid-in capital and no blocked escrow account requirement. The total stated capital must be specified in the Articles of Incorporation, and each member's subscribed contribution must be fully paid before the incorporation registration is accepted: cash contributions must be deposited into a bank account in the name of the company under incorporation, and non-cash contributions must be fully transferred and evidenced by an independent valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the proposed company, Yuhan Hoesa (Yuhan LLC), has been organized as a limited liability company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, and the Articles of Incorporation have been duly executed by the founding members and notarized; WHEREAS all founding members have subscribed to the total capital in the amounts set opposite their respective names in the Contribution Schedule; WHEREAS capital contributions have been or shall be immediately deposited into a bank account established in the name of the company under incorporation, and a Contribution Deposit Certificate will be delivered to the competent registration authority; WHEREAS the directors named in the Articles of Incorporation constitute the first board of directors and are authorized to adopt this First Board Resolution; NOW THEREFORE, the board of directors resolves as follows: 1. The total issued and paid-in capital of the Company is confirmed as the aggregate of the contributions set out in the Contribution Schedule, expressed in Korean won. Each contribution interest shall be recorded in the Member Register, and the capital accounts of the Company shall reflect such contributions. 2. The registered office of the Company is adopted at the full address in the Republic of Korea stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Executive Officer is directed to file the corporate registration, obtain the corporate seal, and complete all formalities necessary for the Company to acquire legal personality. 3. The Representative Executive Officer and the Financial Officer are jointly and severally authorized, with two authorized signatories or one signatory within the internal monetary threshold, to open, maintain and operate commercial bank accounts at any licensed bank in the Republic of Korea, to execute payment orders, treasury transactions, foreign exchange transactions, internet banking mandates and account closing instructions, and to accept loans or guarantees only upon separate board authorization. 4. The Representative Executive Officer is appointed as the statutory representative of the Company. All directors and officers are confirmed in their respective appointments, and such directors and officers are authorized to execute contracts, issue contribution certificates, employ staff, engage auditors, and represent the Company in litigation and administrative proceedings. 5. The Representative Executive Officer is directed to adopt an official corporate seal, prepare and maintain statutory registers, keep accounting records, and make all registrations and filings required by the Commercial Act and applicable tax law. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public licensed under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea, or a notarial office specializing in corporate formation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in the statutory form, setting out the corporate name, business purpose, total stated capital, registered office, contribution value allocated to each member, number of directors, appointment of the Representative Executive Officer, and the method of publication. Every founding member or its lawful attorney must execute the Articles and affix the corporate or personal seal or signature. Foreign corporate members must provide certified abstracts of their corporate existence, a board resolution authorizing participation, and necessary legalization or apostille. The notary will verify identity, legal capacity, signing authority and consistency with the Commercial Act, after which the notary issues a certified duplicate of the notarized Articles for submission to the registry.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation executed by all founding members
Passport or national identity card of each individual member and officer
Certificate of incorporation, board resolution and apostilled public document for any corporate member
Power of attorney or board resolution appointing the local formation agent
Proof of the registered office address, such as a lease agreement or landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses notarization or issues a query, correct the specific defect in member authority, translation, legalization or address proof, then re-submit the revised documents with supplemental declarations. If legalization is incomplete, obtain the required apostille or consular authentication and re-present the dossier within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Capital Contributions and Bank Deposit Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed domestic commercial bank branch in the Republic of Korea where the company-under-incorporation capital account is opened.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After execution of the Articles, establish a capital contribution collection account at a licensed Korean bank in the name of the company under incorporation or in the name of the incorporator acting for the company. Each member must remit the full amount of the contribution subscribed in the Articles, and the bank branch manager must issue a Contribution Deposit Certificate confirming the amount held. Contributions in kind must be transferred completely and supported by an independent appraisal or valuation report. No escrow account is required, but the paid capital must be verifiable before the court registration filing is accepted. The retained certificate and remittance records form part of the registration evidence.
required_dossiers: Company-under-incorporation account opening application and bank due diligence forms
Member remittance records and source-of-funds declarations
Bank-issued Contribution Deposit Certificate
Independent valuation report and asset transfer instrument for non-cash contributions
Contribution Schedule approved by all members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds or imposes anti-money laundering requests, promptly provide updated KYC documents, corporate structure chart, source-of-funds declaration and confirmatory board resolutions. If a certificate is delayed, use another licensed bank branch or escalate to the branch compliance officer with a written explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Registration at the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, or the District Court Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the Company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of incorporation within the statutory period after notarization of the Articles of Incorporation. The application must be submitted with the certified duplicate of the notarized Articles, the Contribution Deposit Certificate, evidence of non-cash contribution valuation, consent letters of the directors and the Representative Executive Officer, proof of the registered office, and payment receipts for registration tax, local education tax and court fees. The registrar verifies the company name, business purpose, capital structure, officers, office address and compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon acceptance, the registry assigns a registration number and records the incorporation date, which is when the Company obtains legal personality.
required_dossiers: Application for corporation registration
Certified duplicate of notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank-issued Contribution Deposit Certificate
In-kind valuation report and transfer documents, if any
Consent letters of directors, auditor and Representative Executive Officer
Proof of the registered office address
Payment receipts for registration tax, education tax and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order or a suspension notice, prepare supplementary notarized documents, corrected forms or additional evidence within the period stated in the notice, not exceeding two weeks. If the application is rejected, file an objection with the same registry and, if necessary, seek an appeal or administrative litigation through legal counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Business Registration and Post-Incorporation Administrative Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, using the HomeTax online portal or in-person window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration is complete, register the Company for taxation with the competent National Tax Service district office. Submit the business registration application setting out the principal business as software development, information security services and cloud cybersecurity SaaS. Obtain the business registration certificate, register for corporate tax and value-added tax, and retain tax invoice issuance capability. The Company must also establish its corporate seal, open an operating bank account, and complete the administrative filings required for employer registration if it hires staff. For pure digital services under ISIC 6201, no industrial operating permit or environmental license is required, but the business registration must accurately describe the digital nature of the services.
required_dossiers: Court registration certificate and registered company number
Certificate of corporate seal
Business registration application form
Tenant lease or registered office documentation
Identification and resident documents of the directors
Bank account certificate or operating account details
Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business category or scope, align the Korean Standard Industrial Classification code with the SaaS security services scope, amend the Articles of Incorporation if necessary, and re-file the corrected application. If penalties are assessed, pay them promptly and request written confirmation of the corrected registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Implementation and Operational Readiness for the SaaS Cybersecurity Business
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company management, external Korean corporate counsel, and the financial institution where the operating account is opened.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene or execute the First Board Resolution to ratify the incorporation steps, confirm the registered office, authorize the opening of operational bank accounts, issue contribution certificates, adopt the official corporate seal, and implement the statutory registers required by the Commercial Act. The Company should also adopt internal information security and personal information protection policies in line with the Personal Information Protection Act, because cybersecurity and SaaS clients will require contractual evidence of governance. The directors must approve the annual corporate compliance calendar covering corporate filings, financial statements, member meetings and statutory record maintenance. For this pure digital service company, no environmental impact assessment, civil defense fire permit or industrial manufacturing license is applicable.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution and supporting consents
Bank account opening package and signing mandates
Corporate seal registration certificate
Statutory registers: member register, director register, auditor register and meeting minutes
Data protection and information security policies for cybersecurity SaaS operations
Registered office records and annual compliance calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or counterparty questions the governance documents, provide a certified copy of the corporate registration, the First Board Resolution and the identity evidence of the authorized signatories. If the legal counsel identifies a defect in the governance file, execute a curative written consent or supplemental board resolution and notarize or apostille it as required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. This is a pure digital cloud cybersecurity SaaS entity under ISIC 6201 and no Korean industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing agency has jurisdiction over the SaaS activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No sectoral operating or manufacturing permit is required for the cybersecurity SaaS business; the National Tax Service business registration certificate is a fiscal registration, not an industrial operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. No manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity is carried out, so the Korean environmental protection authorities have no EIA jurisdiction over this entity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. There is no EIA registration, full EIA report or preliminary environmental review trigger for a pure ISIC 6201 software service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There are no wastewater discharges, volatile organic compound emissions or hazardous waste generation from the SaaS activity, and therefore no quantitative compliance threshold is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the digital SaaS activity. If the Company later leases physical office premises, the building owner must supply the current building fire safety certification, and the Company must complete the workplace safety and health management duties under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including accident prevention plans and employee safety training. No Civil Defense permit is triggered by an office-based information security company.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with electronic tax administration via the HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) and administrative support from the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered place of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Yuhan Hoesa LLC, the company's representative files a business registration application with the competent district tax office after incorporation. Supporting documents include the articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, registered address or lease agreement, and owner's identification. The tax office issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number that simultaneously constitutes the corporation's TIN and VAT registration ID. For a foreign non-resident entity with no Korean domestic place of business that supplies digital services or other taxable goods or services in Korea, the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative and register through the NTS HomeTax portal under the special simplified foreign business registration procedure; the issued foreign business registration number is then used for VAT filings, zero-rated export substantiation, and electronic tax invoices. Changes in business status or registered place of business must be updated on HomeTax within the statutory period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean resident domestic corporation liable to corporate income tax on worldwide income and is not eligible for pass-through taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under Korean check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election rules. A qualifying domestic parent corporation may apply for group taxation with its wholly-owned Korean subsidiaries subject to NTS approval under the statutory consolidated filing conditions, but this is an entity-level filing regime rather than a pass-through election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean VAT Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based VAT registration threshold applies to Korean VAT. Every supplier carrying on business in Korea by selling goods or services must register with the NTS. A foreign supplier of digital services, SaaS, or other taxable supplies to Korean non-registered recipients has a mandatory VAT registration requirement from the first Korean supply; no low-value exemption or KRW-turnover threshold is available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue a tax invoice for each taxable supply, and electronic tax invoices must be issued through the NTS HomeTax e-tax invoice system. E-tax invoice data are transmitted to the NTS in real time upon issuance for every taxable supply, and the NTS operates a mandatory e-tax invoice validation and matching anti-fraud control. High-volume taxpayers and platform operators may transmit invoices through NTS-required API integrations or licensed e-tax invoice service providers, but every invoice must carry the valid NTS e-tax invoice number and the issuer and recipient Business Registration Numbers. Korea does not operate a legacy fiscal stamp clearance mechanism; the real-time electronic tax invoice transmission itself is the statutory anti-fraud digital clearance mechanism. Foreign electronic service suppliers registered under the simplified foreign business VAT registration must also issue electronic tax invoices through HomeTax.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the VAT Act for goods that are physically exported from Korea and for certain services supplied to a non-resident where the place of supply is outside Korea. For the qualifying cybersecurity SaaS product, the statutory zero-rating criteria are: the recipient must be a non-resident customer, the SaaS services must be consumed or used outside Korea, the contract and invoices must identify the offshore recipient, the payment must be received through foreign-exchange-recognized settlement channels, and contemporaneous evidence must prove that the service was supplied outside Korea. Digital services supplied to a resident Korean non-registered customer are taxable at 10% and do not qualify for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Final commercial invoice and international sales contract or service agreement
Foreign exchange transaction proof and bank SWIFT remittance records
Service delivery and offshore-use evidence for SaaS such as customer IP addresses, geo-location logs, server records, and statement of work documentation
NTS e-tax invoice issued at zero percent for the qualifying export supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS applies intensive audit review to zero-rated export claims by cross-matching customs declarations, foreign exchange settlement records, e-tax invoices, and service delivery documentation. If any required export document is missing, inaccurate, or inconsistent, the zero-rated treatment is disallowed and the full 10% VAT is assessed with statutory interest and penalty taxes. Fraudulent, forged, or intentionally manipulated export documents are treated as unlawful tax refund claims and tax evasion, leading to additional penalty assessments, retrospective clawback, criminal prosecution, and fines or imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. The statutory collection period is five years generally, extended to ten years for intentional or fraudulent tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary and exchange-rate authority, with foreign exchange policy administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and executed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act through licensed foreign exchange banks reporting to the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but monitored convertible-currency regime. The won is fully convertible for current-account transactions such as import settlements, royalty payments, and software-as-a-service subscription fees, where authorization is effectively automatic once the underlying commercial contract and invoice are submitted to a licensed foreign exchange bank. Capital-account transactions, including non-resident equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, and repatriation of capital gains or loan principal, require ex ante or ex post reporting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; in practice, inbound foreign direct investment is safeguarded by ex post verification rather than licensing, provided the foreign investment is reported within three months of capital inflow. Profit and dividend remittance to non-resident shareholders is permissible after corporate tax settlement, supported by audited financial statements, board dividend resolution, and a foreign exchange purchase record at a domestic bank. However, practical hurdles remain: financial institutions expect documentary proof of the underlying business purpose, source of funds for the capital injection, and consistency between the declared ISIC 6201 cybersecurity SaaS activities and the payment flows. Cross-border settlement must be routed through a bank possessing a foreign exchange dealing license; unauthorized electronic money institutions or overseas payment firms cannot provide permanent corporate treasury settlement as primary bank accounts. Overall, convertibility is high for compliant current-account flows, while capital flows remain subject to detailed documentation and reporting discipline.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Regulations, export proceeds must be received and settled within the statutory receipt period prescribed by the BOK for the relevant export category, with the general expectation that proceeds are recovered within the timeline stated in the export declaration and subject to extension only for documented cause. There is no blanket mandatory percentage conversion into Korean won; the exporter may hold foreign currency in a domestic foreign-currency account, but the receipt must be reported to the licensed foreign exchange bank via the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) without undue delay, and any conversion into won must be executed through a domestic bank with a foreign exchange dealing license. For the Yuhan Hoesa cybersecurity SaaS model, export receipts consist largely of subscription fees which are treated as service export proceeds and are not subject to compulsory surrender ratios; the treasury must nevertheless maintain a perfect reconciliation file between each inbound SWIFT credit and the corresponding export invoice in order to clear FEIS reporting and bank compliance review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Current Account (KRW) and Foreign Currency Current Account (USD/EUR/JPY)
Capital Escrow Account and SWIFT-enabled Operational Foreign Currency Account
Operational Currency Account with FEIS Reporting Integration
Corporate Settlement Account with Trade and Investment Dedicated Relationship Desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is low for offshore fintech EMIs as the primary treasury settlement rail. Under the Banking Act, only licensed banks may accept KRW deposits; under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, money transfer services beyond payment collection require registration as licensed e-money issuers or payment gateways and are not permitted to maintain corporate operating accounts or provide foreign exchange sweeping services without a foreign exchange dealing license. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise or Payoneer can be used narrowly as invoice collection agents or disbursement tools in external markets, but they lack local branch presence and cannot discharge Korean statutory capital verification, FEIS reports, or bank-level KYC obligations. Consequently, the determining rail must be a Tier-1 Korean commercial bank, with EMIs limited to ancillary functions such as collecting overseas SaaS subscription proceeds from non-Korean clients, provided the flows are separately reconciled and justified under the entity's treasury policy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is not strictly mandatory for non-resident directors under current FATF-aligned Korean rules, but the designating corporate officer or the registered domestic contact must complete a non-face-to-face customer identification procedure using video interview combined with certificates issued by a licensed public certificate authority. Where the director is outside Korea, remote consular proxy opening is not a standard statutory route; instead, the bank accepts notarized and apostilled board resolutions, director identification, and power-of-attorney documents, followed by a recorded video call with the principal. For Capital Escrow accounts, Korean banks frequently require an in-person or notarized face-to-face identity confirmation at the branch or at an Overseas Korean Embassy notary office; the highest onboarding viability is achieved when at least one local authorized signatory resident in Korea attends the branch interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership where non-resident shareholders are recorded through proxy or offshore nominee layers without a transparent organizational chart.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the corporate register, apostilled Certificate of Incorporation, formal board resolution appointing local directors, complete shareholder register disclosing each natural-person UBO holding above 25%, identity documents of all UBOs, and a notarized statement of source of funds for the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds concern arising from rapid non-resident capital injection with no historical profitability or clear business justification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of personal or corporate bank statements in the investor's name, a signed business plan for the ISIC 6201 cybersecurity SaaS operation, evidence of prior open-source software or penetration-testing business activity, and a tax clearance certificate from the shareholder's country of residence demonstrating legitimate earnings capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media and sanctions screening hits or jurisdiction risk associated with the foreign investor or target client region for cybersecurity export services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party sanctions and adverse-media screening runs for each director, shareholder, and counterparty against OFAC, EU, and UN lists; position paper explaining any name-match hits; end-client IT environments and target countries evidencing no prohibited defence, military, or critical infrastructure use; and a signed use-case attestation for the cloud vulnerability scanning SaaS output.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the declared cybersecurity SaaS business model and requested payment flows, such as large inbound funding to KRW account before customer contracts are evidenced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master subscription agreements or service orders with international clients, commercial invoices and actual payment institution statements, SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificates showing the entity's genuine operational standing, a current contractual pipeline report, and a sworn board declaration confirming that disbursements will be used solely for development, cloud hosting, compliance licensing, and permitted trade payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound non-resident capital injection for equity subscription must be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank using a high-value SWIFT MT103 wire with the remitter named as the true investor, not an intermediary shell. The purpose of payment should be stated as equity investment in Korean limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) with reference to the Foreign Investment Report. After receipt, the investor must submit the capital injection to the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) through the bank within the statutory reporting window, generally three months for inward foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The bank will issue a Foreign Currency Clearance Certificate or Capital Verification Statement confirming the won conversion, after which the amount is posted to the Capital Escrow Account and verified against the authorized capital stated in the articles of incorporation; the certificate is mandatory for subsequent registration and dividend remittance purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the cybersecurity SaaS operation will primarily settle through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for service fees, software subscriptions, cloud infrastructure charges, and licensing payments, each supported by an invoice and underlying contract and cleared through the correspondent banking network of the Korean Tier-1 bank. For larger multi-jurisdictional deployments or hardware-related components, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (L/C) at sight or deferred payment terms is appropriate, while documentary collections are acceptable for low-risk open-account transactions with trusted service providers. All disbursements exceeding the bank's foreign exchange limit require purpose-code declaration and supporting documentation in FEIS; the treasury desk must maintain invoice-versus-clearing reconciliation files to support tax and AML audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla forward foreign exchange contracts with licensed Korean banks for committed SaaS subscription and disbursement receivables or payables denominated in USD, EUR, or JPY, subject to t+3 confirmation and documentation of the underlying exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the Korean won exposure is booked against a non-resident counterparty and the underlying trade or treasury commitment is evidenced; eligibility is highly constrained and requires the bank's FX desk approval

Cross-currency interest rate swaps solely for hedges of long-term offshore debt or capital lease obligations, prohibited for speculative purposes under Korean FX regulation; all hedging instruments require adherence to FEIS reporting and Board-approved treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment for the previous fiscal year, including the 10% local income tax component
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via HomeTax; the local income tax surcharge is remitted with the local government through the local tax e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities: file and pay by 31 March of the following year; for non-calendar fiscal years: within three months after fiscal year-end; if the deadline falls on a non-business day, the next business day applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or under-reporting triggers a negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax (40% in evasion cases), plus daily overdue interest of 0.022%; continued non-payment authorises enforced collection, tax liens, VAT business-registration cancellation, and for dormant entities, court-initiated strike-off of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities: due by 31 August each year covering the first six months; for non-calendar fiscal years: due within two months after the end of the first half of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay interim tax, or underpayment, accrues 0.022% daily late-payment interest and an additional 20% under-reporting penalty; the final corporate income tax settlement reconciles the interim payment, and persistent non-payment may trigger enforced collection and administrative closure of the tax registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First quarter (January-March): due 25 April; third quarter (July-September): due 25 October; same deadlines apply to a Yuhan Hoesa with a calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay the preliminary VAT return results in a 10% or 20% negligence penalty depending on intent, daily interest of 0.022%, and possible cancellation of the VAT business registration after persistent non-reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (January-June): due 25 July of the same year; second half (July-December): due 25 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or deficient VAT filing incurs a 10% or 20% negligence penalty, 0.022% daily late-payment interest, and tax-invoice penalties for incorrect or missing invoices; serious recurrence can lead to VAT registration cancellation and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report Submission, if the company meets the mandatory audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the OpenDART filing system; audited financial statements also form part of the tax return documentation submitted to the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: the audited financial statements must be approved and the audit report submitted to the Financial Supervisory Service by 31 March, or by 30 April where an extension is lawfully applied under the Act on External Audit of Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a statutory audit or to file the audit report is punishable by administrative fines of up to KRW 20 million; the Financial Supervisory Service may order a special audit, restrict share issuances, and recommend criminal penalties for directors and officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Confirmation and Share-Transfer Change Report, if the entity is a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy; share-transfer changes must be filed with the reporting bank or KOTRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation, where applicable, is due within six months after fiscal year-end; any transfer of shares or membership interests affecting foreign ownership must be reported within 30 days after the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a foreign-investment change report or annual confirmation can result in administrative fines up to KRW 2 million, forfeiture of foreign-invested enterprise privileges, and adverse tax-treaty withholding outcomes; chronic non-reporting may cause KOTRA to revoke foreign-investment registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent CPA audit applies to a South Korean Yuhan Hoesa when total assets at the end of the fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion. Listed companies and financial institutions are audited regardless of size. There is no separate turnover or headcount audit trigger for an ordinary unlisted, non-financial Yuhan Hoesa; however, banks, investors, or a government designation under a Presidential Decree may require an audit or agreed-upon procedures even if the asset threshold is not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Audited financial statements must be prepared under K-IFRS for listed entities, or under K-GAAP and the Korean Simplified Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Companies for unlisted entities; all audits are performed in accordance with the Korean Standards on Auditing issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a central public UBO register for ordinary Yuhan Hoesa entities. The statutory confirmation mechanism is the member register, which must be updated without delay upon any transfer of membership interests; if the company qualifies as a foreign-invested enterprise, any change in foreign shareholding or beneficial ownership must be reported to KOTRA or the reporting bank within 30 days of the transaction. There is no separate annual UBO filing for purely domestic ownership, but the National Tax Service may request a beneficial-ownership declaration in tax-treaty and anti-money-laundering examinations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (member registry showing contributions, transfers, ownership percentages, and dates)
Register of Directors and management council members
Register of Charges/Mortgages over company assets
Minute Book of member meetings and management council resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,000 per year for a registered Seoul office and compliance agent; USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per year when outsourced corporate secretarial support is included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 20,000 - USD 60,000 for a statutory certified audit of a Korean Yuhan Hoesa that exceeds the KRW 12 billion asset threshold; no statutory audit fee is legally incurred below that threshold unless a bank, investor, or government designation requires one.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national headline rate, plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate tax, giving an aggregate maximum effective rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive national schedule: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% above KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion. Tax holidays under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act: qualifying high-tech foreign-investment cybersecurity SaaS can obtain 100% corporate tax exemption for 3 years and a 50% reduction for the next 2 years in a Free Economic Zone. Special Tax Treatment Control Act incentives include an R&D tax credit on qualifying software-development expenses (incremental credit up to 25%), SME employment-related credits, and technology transfer benefits if the Korean entity owns and directly exploits the penetration-testing software and maintains contemporaneous R&D documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return on the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal, accompanied by local income tax surtax schedules and supplementary non-resident withholding and transfer pricing forms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one return per fiscal year), plus half-year intermediate prepayment for calendar-year corporations and monthly withholding filings for employees and non-residents.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; a calendar-year entity files by March 31. External-audit companies may extend by one month to April 30. If the ordinary or extended deadline falls on a weekend, filing is timely on the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identity and business registration: company name, representative director, business registration number, corporate address, fiscal year, tax office, and status of domestic place of business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Korean place-of-business code and the foreign ultimate parent identity. A non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa must designate a statutory representative in Korea for service of tax documents; if the representative field is left blank, NTS may treat the return as not filed and impose non-filing penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement summary: gross revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, selling and administrative expenses, non-operating income and expenses, and ordinary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Korean-source income attributable to the cybersecurity SaaS activity performed through the Korean entity or PE. Revenue from penetration-testing applications sold to overseas users must be apportioned carefully; bundled license, implementation, maintenance, and cloud-hosting income must be split into royalty and service components for withholding and transfer pricing purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation and add-back adjustments: non-deductible expenses, entertainment expense limits, fines and penalties, depreciation differences, unrealized gains, tax-exempt or reduced income, and prior-period audit adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back parent-brand royalties and management fees if they lack a valid calculation basis, properly withhold 22% WHT, and document the arm's-length substantiation. Foreign exchange losses from intercompany loans are deductible only if commercial terms exist; the non-resident shareholder should maintain signed agreements, board minutes, and invoice counterparties before the transaction occurs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforwards: enter current profit, subtract deductible tax-loss carryforwards within the statutory expiry period, and derive the final taxable income to which the progressive bracket rates are applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly formed cybersecurity SaaS LLC, the 5-year loss carryforward can monetize early R&D and implementation deficits; preserve loss schedules with supporting returns and avoid a change of business purpose or aggregation that would break continuity. Loss claims of a shell entity with no employees, contracts, or substantive assets will be challenged as paper losses and disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate tax computation: progressive bracket application, foreign tax credit, R&D credits, minimum tax rules, and deduction of advance/prepayment installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean company receives dividends from foreign subsidiaries, include the indirect foreign-tax-credit schedules and attach the foreign dividend and foreign tax credit form. For non-resident shareholders, do not credit the 22% dividend WHT against the Korean corporate tax unless that shareholder itself maintains a Korean permanent establishment; NTS will reject the direct credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surtax and net tax payable: 10% surtax on the national corporate tax, deductions for withheld taxes and prepayments, and final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must deposit the local income tax surtax even where a DTA lowers the national tax; treaty relief does not automatically reduce the Korean local surtax unless the specific treaty covers Korean local tax. Attach a reconciliation if a withholding agent remitted the statutory 22% amount and the treaty-reduced rate was subsequently proven; refunds are processed after the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident and transfer pricing schedules: shareholder composition, dividends paid to non-residents, royalties and interest paid to non-residents, intercompany transaction values, transfer pricing methods, and DTA treaty relief claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach contemporaneous Local File and the transfer pricing disclosure form if the KRW 10 billion threshold is exceeded. Declare each non-resident payee as beneficial owner and certify that a Tax Residency Certificate has been received. If a treaty claim is made retroactively after the withholding date, NTS requires a refund proceeding; failure to obtain proper supporting documents triggers a 20% under-withholding penalty and the 22% statutory rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 20% of the unpaid tax where no return is filed under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2. Unfaithful or understated filing: 20% of the under-reported tax; fraudulent under-reporting or unlawful refund claim: 40% under Article 47-3. Late payment interest accrues at 0.022% per day on the deficient amount from the statutory due date to the payment date. Criminal tax evasion where the evaded amount exceeds KRW 300 million is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to 3 times the tax evaded. NTS may also publicly blacklist the company as a high-amount chronic delinquent taxpayer, which blocks government contracts, trade licenses, and bank credit facilities.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% for cash dividends paid by a Korean resident corporation to a non-resident corporation (20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA, the non-resident shareholder must submit before the distribution date: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign revenue authority for the relevant year; (2) the National Tax Service application form for reduction or exemption of non-resident withholding tax; (3) a beneficial ownership declaration confirming that the shareholder is not a conduit and receives the dividend for its own account; and (4) shareholding period evidence where the treaty condition requires at least 10% or 25% ownership for a 12-month period. If documents are late, the withholding agent must retain 22%; a refund may be claimed through the non-resident annual return or a domestic refund procedure, but NTS applies document-validation audits and interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Korean payer to a non-resident for software licenses, trademarks, know-how, or technical services are Korean-source income subject to statutory 22% WHT (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Treaty rates generally reduce royalties to 10% and interest to 10-15% depending on the treaty and arm's-length financial terms. The same DTA protocol applies: TRC, beneficial ownership, and executed loan/licence agreements confirming arm's-length rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate international related-party transactions (with all foreign related parties) triggers contemporaneous Local File preparation; KRW 100 billion triggers Master File; CbC report obligations arise when the consolidated MNE group has at least KRW 1.2 trillion gross revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has not enacted the Cayman or UK-style Economic Substance Regulations in the domestic code, but substance is legally required through the general anti-avoidance rule, substance-over-form doctrine, and DTA benefit denial rules. The NTS applies a Core Income-Generating Activities analysis to the cybersecurity SaaS entity: employees and managers actually performing R&D,
